hypothesis: If Thompson's similitude argument holds, an animal in steady lift-supported flight or glide must move at least at v_min = sqrt(2 W / (rho S C_Lmax)), and across animals of roughly similar design the characteristic airspeed scales with wing loading W/S to the power 1/2 (equivalently, under isometry, with linear size to the power 1/2 and with body mass to the power 1/6).

interpretations.reading: Across lift-supported fliers and gliders, characteristic airspeed v scales with wing loading Q = W/S as v ~ Q^0.5 (ch02-06 first half, ch02-10).
interpretations.why: The exponent follows from the lift equation only if C_L and air density are the same across taxa; whether real animals satisfy that is empirical.

interpretations.reading: A flying fish in a steady glide moves at or above its own minimum lift-supported speed computed from its measured wing loading and measured maximum lift coefficient.
interpretations.why: A consistency check of the fish against the model; needs measured W, S, C_Lmax and airspeed.

interpretations.reading: Power required for level flight P_req = W v_min / (L/D)_max exceeds muscle power available P_avail = m_muscle * p_specific for the flying fish at its size (ch02-07 reading: beyond some size muscle-powered flight is impossible).
interpretations.why: Needs a sourced muscle mass fraction and a sourced mass-specific muscle power; if either is unsourced the verdict is cannot-tell.

interpretations.reading: Given W ~ L^3, S ~ L^2, constant C_L and rho, then v_min ~ L^0.5 and P_req ~ L^3.5 while P_avail ~ L^3.
interpretations.why: A mathematical consequence of the stated definitions; goes to the Lean thread via physics/FORMAL-STATEMENTS.md, not tested on data here.

pass_criterion: Pre-registered. Interpretation A: pool every taxon in physics/glide-data.csv and physics/comparison-data.csv that has a measured body weight W (N), a measured lifting area S (m^2) and a measured steady airspeed v (m/s) from a fetched source (field, video or wind tunnel; simulations excluded; one row per species, the median if several). Ordinary least squares of log10 v on log10 (W/S). SUPPORTS if n >= 5 taxa spanning at least one decade of W/S AND the 95% CI of the slope contains 0.5 AND excludes 0. Interpretation B: INSIDE the envelope if the flying fish's measured airspeed range overlaps [v_min, 3 v_min] with v_min = sqrt(2 W / (rho S C_Lmax)), rho = 1.225 kg m^-3, C_Lmax the measured maximum lift coefficient from a wind-tunnel source, W and S from the same species or genus. Interpretation C: INSIDE if P_avail >= P_req using only sourced values.
fail_criterion: Pre-registered. Interpretation A: REFUTES if n >= 5 AND the 95% CI of the slope excludes 0.5. INCONCLUSIVE (underpowered) if n < 5, or the CI width exceeds 1.0, or the W/S range spans less than one decade. Interpretation B: OUTSIDE if the entire measured airspeed range lies below v_min (the glide could not be lift-supported) or above 3 v_min; CANNOT TELL if any of W, S, C_Lmax or airspeed lacks a measured value with a fetched source. Interpretation C: OUTSIDE if P_avail < P_req with sourced inputs; CANNOT TELL otherwise. MIXED if interpretations disagree in sign.

holdout_rule: Class Aves is the frozen holdout (holdout/exam.json) and this claim is listed there as a bird-only claim. No bird row is read, fitted or plotted. The kickoff's comparison set named birds; they are excluded here as a deviation and the hub has been asked to confirm.
interpretation: Thompson's 'linear dimensions' l is replaced by the directly measurable wing loading W/S, which is what his own derivation (momentum balance over the wing area) actually uses; l^0.5 follows only under isometry (W ~ l^3, S ~ l^2). 'Speed' is the steady glide or cruising airspeed, not the launch speed. 'Work of flight' is the mechanical power required for level flight at v_min. Air density is taken as sea-level standard. The flying fish is a glider; interpretation C asks the hypothetical question whether its muscles could power level flight, which is what #43 and the Darwin claim need.
already_seen_before_preregistration: Makiguchi et al. 2013 (10.3354/ab00494) full text: fork length 25.7-34.0 cm, body mass 178-263 g for 13 Cypselurus heterurus doederleini; estimated leap speed 3.87-5.15 m/s; pitch 20.0 +- 3.3 deg.

Abstracts only: Davenport 1994 (approach ~10 m/s, taxiing up to 50 beats/s), Deng et al. 2019 CFD (C_Lmax 1.05, L/D max 4.7, predicted 45.4 m and 13.2 m; simulation, not used as data), Park and Choi 2010 (L/D max near 0 deg, C_L largest at 30-35 deg; glide performance comparable to some bird wings), Fish 1990 (fin area and span increase with mass).
No wing loading, lifting area or C_Lmax value had been read for any taxon when this file was written; no comparison-taxon value had been read.

caveats: Thompson's muscle-power-as-l^3 premise is itself an assumption (constant mass-specific power); modern work treats it as size-dependent. Recorded in physics/FORMAL-STATEMENTS.md as an assumption, not tested here.

W, S and C_Lmax are from 0.04-0.06 kg stuffed specimens of one species; the airspeed range is a second-hand field figure for larger flying fish of several genera. The pre-registration allowed same species or genus; the field figure is at family level, so this verdict rests on an assumption the pre-registration did not foresee and is reported with that weakness.

changes: Exocoetidae is explicitly in the interpretation-A set: its rows come from physics/glide-data.csv; the comparison lineages come from physics/comparison-data.csv.

Gliders (Exocoetidae, Pteromyini, Cynocephalidae) and powered fliers (Chiroptera, Diptera) are two physical regimes. The interpretation-A regression is run separately for each group, and each group needs n >= 5 taxa spanning one decade of W/S for a verdict; a pooled fit is reported only as a secondary descriptive number and decides nothing.

Thompson's claim is stated for a bird in powered level flight; applying v_min to a glider assumes only the lift balance W = 0.5 rho v^2 S C_L, which holds for any steady lift-supported flight. That is the sense in which it applies to gliders.
values_read_between_preregistration_and_: Park and Choi 2010 Table 1 (five Cypselurus hiraii specimens: SL 199-209 mm, mass 0.04-0.06 kg, pectoral area 5498-7069 mm2, pelvic 1603-1837 mm2, body planform 4258-4640 mm2, span 233-261 mm, AR 9.0-10.7) and Table 2 (C_Lmax 0.78 at 35 deg, L/D max 4.37 at 0 deg, reference area A1+A2+A3); field flight speed 10-20 m/s quoted there from Hertel 1966, Fish 1990, Davenport 1994.

Bahlman et al. 2013: Glaucomys sabrinus reference mass 92.7 g, published wing loading 59 N/m2 (Stafford et al.), average glide velocity 7.2 m/s over 18 m glides, launch 5.4 m/s; mammalian glider wing loadings 38-143 N/m2.

Byrnes et al. 2008: Galeopterus variegatus 0.75-1.4 kg (mean 1.1 kg), asymptotic horizontal glide velocity 9.91-10.2 m/s (mean 10.1) for glides over 20 m, landing 3.99 m/s, take-off 0.61-8.2 m/s (mean 3.70).
Davenport 1992 and 2003 abstracts: allometric exponents for Exocoetus obtusirostris (mass b=2.981, lateral fin area b=1.834, wing loading b=1.236 on standard length); no absolute values read.
No bat or fly value had been read when this amendment was written.
